segments.source: Innovation, in contrast, is the introduction of new ideas, of new ways or approaches that change how things were done before. segments.source: MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) is a technological standard used to transfer up to 16 information channels. It transfers messages of events that include musical notation, tone and speed among other things. Basically, this files explain what notes are played, when, for how long and how loud.
segments.en: MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) is a standard for exchanging musical messages. A MIDI 1.0 stream supports 16 channels. Messages describe events such as a note starting or stopping, its pitch and its velocity. Essentially, the file specifies which notes to play, when and for how long; it does not contain a sound recording.
segments.es: MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) es un estándar para intercambiar mensajes musicales. Un flujo MIDI 1.0 admite 16 canales. Los mensajes describen eventos como el inicio y fin de una nota, su altura y su velocidad de pulsación. En esencia, el archivo indica qué notas tocar, cuándo y durante cuánto tiempo; no contiene la grabación del sonido.

segments.source: and are essentially two separate models that are trained together with an opposed purpose. One of the models, the generator, generates new data samples from a random seed; the second model, the discriminator, tries to tell whether the data is original (real) or if it was created by the generative model (fake). Due to their behavior, they are typicall compared to a counterfeiter and a cop. The counterfeiter keeps improving the quality of the works while the cop gets better at detecting which ones are real or faked.
segments.en: and consist of two models trained together with opposing goals. The generator creates new samples from random input; the discriminator tries to distinguish them from real data. They are often compared to a counterfeiter and a police officer: as one improves the fakes, the other gets better at spotting them.
segments.es: y son esencialmente dos modelos separados que se entrenan juntos con un propósito opuesto. Uno de los modelos, el generador, genera nuevas muestras de datos a partir de una semilla aleatoria; el segundo modelo, el discriminador, intenta decir si los datos son originales (reales) o si fueron creados por el modelo generativo (falso). Debido a su comportamiento, normalmente se les compara con un falsificador y un policía. El falsificador sigue mejorando la calidad de las obras mientras el policía mejora en detectar cuáles son reales o falsas.

segments.en: The structure of a GAN fed with doinus.
segments.es: La estructura de una GAN alimentada con doinus.

editorialReview.scope: Full Spanish and English page review; active rendered text and metadata

segments.source: Basically, during the training process, the counterfeiter should get much better at creating new data (in this case images of new possible doinus) while the cop should improve at the detection of fake doinus, forcing the improvement of the counterfeiter. At some point, the generative model should be good enough at creating doinus that it would become absolutely impossible for the discriminative model to discern among real or fake doinus, meaning we have a model capable of creating good enough doinus.
segments.en: During training, the generator tries to create representations of new doinus that the discriminator cannot distinguish from real ones. This competition can improve the generated samples, although fooling the discriminator does not by itself guarantee that a person will find the music interesting.
segments.es: Durante el entrenamiento, el generador intenta crear representaciones de nuevos doinus que el discriminador no distinga de las reales. Esa competencia puede mejorar las muestras generadas, aunque engañar al discriminador no garantiza por sí solo que la música resulte interesante para una persona.

segments.source: The images we were trying to create were really sparse, with lots of zeroes and only some ones on the notes being played. The generator initially learnt that by switching all the pixels off, it could trick the dumb discriminator at the beginning. However, during training, at some point, even the dumbest of discriminators was able to detect that a blank image was not a real doinu, which meant that all the efforts made by the generator to produce blank images from noise were now worthless. The generator was not able to adapt fast enough to trick the new discriminator and the training diverged.
segments.en: The images we were trying to create were really sparse, with lots of zeroes and only some ones on the notes being played. The generator initially learnt that by switching all the pixels off, it could trick the dumb discriminator at the beginning. However, during training, at some point, even the dumbest of discriminators was able to detect that a blank image was not a real doinu, which meant that all the efforts made by the generator to produce blank images from noise were now worthless. The generator was not able to adapt fast enough to trick the new discriminator and the training diverged.
segments.es: Las imágenes que intentábamos crear eran muy escasas, con muchos ceros y solo algunos unos en las notas que se tocaban. Inicialmente, el generador aprendió que apagando todos los píxeles, podía engañar al discriminador tonto al principio. Sin embargo, durante el entrenamiento, en algún momento, incluso el discriminador más tonto fue capaz de detectar que una imagen en blanco no era un doinu real, lo que significaba que todos los esfuerzos realizados por el generador para producir imágenes en blanco a partir del ruido ahora eran inútiles. El generador no pudo adaptarse lo suficientemente rápido para engañar al nuevo discriminador y el entrenamiento divergió.

segments.source: The amount of data needed to properly train a GAN is a lot more than we had available, bigger datasets give better results in this kind of networks. Few-shot learning in GANs is a key point being worked on in the academic community right now.
segments.en: We had too little data to train this GAN well. Expanding the dataset helped, although quantity does not replace quality. Few-shot GAN learning was a research direction we wanted to explore.
segments.es: Nos faltaban datos para entrenar bien esta GAN. Ampliar el conjunto nos ayudó, aunque la cantidad no sustituye la calidad. El aprendizaje con pocos ejemplos en GAN era una línea de investigación que nos interesaba explorar.

editorialReview.scope: Spanish and English wording

segments.source: Time is key in training GANs, if the training is stable and there aren’t any divergences, the results keep improving with training time, sometimes getting pretty good results as the training goes on.
segments.en: Training time matters, provided the process is stable. In our experiments, longer stable training improved some results; longer training is not a guarantee of improvement in every case.
segments.es: El tiempo de entrenamiento importa, pero solo si el proceso es estable. En nuestras pruebas, prolongar un entrenamiento estable permitió mejorar algunos resultados; entrenar más tiempo no garantiza una mejora en todos los casos.

editorialReview.scope: Spanish and English wording

segments.source: Simplify the data to be generated and fed to the neural networks as much as possible. Make life easier for your neural networks. Sparse matrices are the devil and should be condensed into a vector if possible, as neural networks love to give outputs full of zeroes if this are available to them.
segments.en: Simplifying the data representation made a crucial difference for us. In this task, converting sparse matrices into vectors reduced the tendency to generate empty outputs. This is a lesson from our experiment, not a universal rule.
segments.es: Simplificar la representación de los datos fue decisivo para nosotros. En este problema, transformar matrices dispersas en vectores redujo la tendencia a producir salidas vacías. No es una regla universal, sino una lección de este experimento.
